newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower, Oct ends over support.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower, Oct ends over support.

text.p: CSCE world October sugar futures ended lower on the day but the benchmark October contract managed to settle over its downside target despite an early breach of support.
The front month closed down 0.08 cent at 11.58 cents a lb, having ranged from 11.68 to 11.55 cents. The back months settled 0.03 to 0.11 cent weaker.
Floor sources said the funds were early sellers in an attempt to erode support at 11.57 in October, where sell stops were thought to be resting.
Steady selling below 11.60 cents in October pressured the contract to the day's low of 11.55 cents. Failing to fall further, the contract climbed off the lows amid light short-covering.

The October contract is expected to test 11.55 cents again on Thursday and climb back toward the recent high if it maintains support. A move below 11.55 cents is likely to attract substantial fund selling, traders said.
"If we get through it's a whole new area," a floor source said. "We could see 11.40-11.20 cents."
Open interest in October rose by 1,394 lots to 112,984 lots as of early Tuesday.
An estimated 14,924 lots changed hands compared with Tuesday's official 19,510 lots.
Mexico's Agroindustry Sugar Committee weekly harvest update put the 1996/97 crop (November-July) at 4,543,851 tonnes with a yield of 10.77 percent.
Output in the previous season reached 4,377,453 tonnes with a yield of 10.89 percent.
